question: The time period of ______ year(s) is taken into account in calculating national income.
solution:
The correct answer is **__one.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National income** of a country means the **sum total of incomes earned by the citizens of that country** during a given **period, over a year.**
 
• The** time period taken into account in calculating national income is usually one year or a fiscal year,** which is the period for which a company or government prepares its financial statements.
 
 
• However, in some cases, a longer period of two years is taken into account to account for fluctuations in economic activity due to seasonal factors, natural disasters, or other exceptional events.
 
• This longer period helps to smooth out the impact of short-term fluctuations and provides a more accurate picture of the overall economic performance of the country.
 
 
 
• **National income **is an important **indicator of a country's economic performance** and is used by policymakers, investors, and analysts to make decisions about economic policies and investments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National income is calculated using various methods**, such as the output method, income method, and expenditure method.

 
 
• **The output method** measures national income by** adding up the value of all goods and services produced** in the country, while the income method measures it by adding up all the income earned by individuals and businesses in the country.
 
• **The expenditure method** measures national income by **adding up all the spending on goods and services** by households, businesses, and the government.
 
• The** income method** measures all the** income earned by all the factors of production** in an economy.
